title: Stylus Haptics Research Database
description: Everything gathered so far about stylus haptics on Android: sources, devices, interfaces, how the pieces work, plans and open questions. Each record says how well its content has been checked.

status_legend.verified: Checked on 2 Nov 2026 against a primary source: official documentation, a project's own page, or the code in this repository.
status_legend.unverified: Taken from the research inventory, vendor specifications, community posts or background knowledge. Not yet checked.
status_legend.inferred: A conclusion drawn from verified facts. Treat it as a working hypothesis.
status_legend.open: Unknown. A gap to close before building on it.

records.title: Stylo2 Haptics repository (this project)

links.label: Upstream project named in the README

records.summary: The Magisk module and companion app behind the XDA thread. It contains the only working third-party client for the Stylo 2 haptics service found so far.
details: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ holds the reconstructed service interface: ISdkAidlInterface, ISDKAidlCallback, Vibration and IpeFeature. The files are marked as cleaned reconstructions.
OplusPencilSdkClient.kt defines StylusVibrationClient: permission check, bindService, interface-descriptor check, and a StateFlow<Connection> for the UI.
The README says the vibration presets were taken from analysis of the stock OnePlus Notes app.
Build: Kotlin, minSdk 30, targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, AGP 8.13.0, Kotlin 2.0.21.
Known defect: unbind() calls stopVibration() after unbindService(), so the stop command can go to a binder that is already released. Stop first, then unbind.
Known defect: getSupportFeatureList() is declared but has no transaction code and always throws.
records.basis: Read in full from the repository on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: XDA: OnePlus Stylo 2 global haptic feedback
records.summary: Discussion and install thread for the Stylo2 Haptics Magisk module and app, which is the project in this repository.
details: The repository README links this thread for discussion and install instructions.

Module: installs the app to /system/priv-app with a privapp-permissions allowlist on the system, system_ext and product partitions, so Android grants it com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT at boot. The README states that no firmware files are modified.
App: binds to com.oplus.ipemanager with the action com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK and calls setVibrationType and startFeedBackVibration.
Tested only on a OnePlus Pad 3 running Global OxygenOS (converted from OPD2413 ColorOS to OPD2415), Android 16.
records.basis: Repository README checked on 2 Nov 2026. The thread itself was not re-read.

records.title: ReVanced issue #180: Stylo 2 haptics in patched StarNote
records.summary: Reports that a patched StarNote build loses Stylo 2 haptics while the unmodified app keeps them.

records.title: xiaomi-sheng-thp (Linux userspace pen and touch driver)
records.summary: Userspace driver for the Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro 12.4 ("sheng") on Linux. It shows pen position coming from the touch controller and pressure coming over Bluetooth.
details: Reads raw THP frames from the NT36532E touch controller through kernel nodes such as /proc/nvt_thp_stylus and exposes standard input devices through uinput.
Pen coordinates, tilt and hover come from the touch controller stream. Pen scanning works only at 60 Hz or 120 Hz panel refresh.
Pressure comes from the pen's Bluetooth HID reports (BlueZ required).
The Focus Pen Pro posture sensor is read separately through libssc.
No haptics support is mentioned.
C++20, Apache-2.0, runs as root, needs a kernel with the Xiaomi THP nodes.
records.basis: Project README read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: com.oplus.ipemanager pen service and binding
records.summary: The OnePlus system service that owns the Stylo 2 link. Apps bind to it, and it does the Bluetooth work.
details: Package: com.oplus.ipemanager
Service: com.oplus.ipemanager/.btadsorb.CoreService
Bind with Intent("com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK").setPackage("com.oplus.ipemanager") and BIND_AUTO_CREATE.
Required permission: com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT. The README calls it a restricted system permission that ordinary apps cannot be granted.
On Android 11 and later the client manifest needs <queries> entries for the package and the action to see the service.
Callers never send Bluetooth packets. The service talks to the pen.
Who gets access (from the README): the stock Notes app holds the permission and binds through a bundled SDK; approved third-party apps use a separate OnePlus developer SDK; any other app is refused.
records.basis: AndroidManifest.xml, OplusPencilSdkClient.kt and README in this repository.

records.title: ISdkAidlInterface: transaction table
records.summary: The Binder interface the pen service returns. Twelve numbered calls cover state queries, vibration control and callback registration.
details: Descriptor: com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISdkAidlInterface
1 getPencilConnectState() returns int
2 getVibrationSwitchState() returns boolean
3 isFunctionVibrationEnable() returns boolean
4 isDemoModeEnable() returns boolean
5 enableDemoMode(boolean)
6 getSuportSdkVersion() returns int (spelled this way in the source)
7 setVibrationType(int)
8 startVibration(int)
9 setISdkAidlCallback(ISDKAidlCallback)
10 unsetISdkAidlCallback(ISDKAidlCallback)
11 startFeedBackVibration()
12 stopFeedBackVibration()
All calls are two-way (flags 0) and read an exception header from the reply. Booleans travel as int 0 or 1.
getSupportFeatureList() returning List<String> is declared in the Java interface but has no transaction code.
records.basis: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ISdkAidlInterface.java

records.title: ISDKAidlCallback: service-to-app events
records.summary: Callback interface an app registers to hear about pen connection and switch changes.
details: Descriptor: com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISDKAidlCallback
1 onConnectionChanged(int state)
2 onVibrationSwitchStateChange(boolean)
3 onFunctionFeedbackStateChange(boolean)
4 onDemoModeEnableChange(boolean)
All four are one-way (FLAG_ONEWAY), so the service never waits on the app.
Registered with transaction 9 and removed with transaction 10. The current app does not register one yet.
records.basis: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ISDKAidlCallback.java

ERASER = 1
BALLPEN = 2

FUNCTION_VIBRATION = 4
The client sends type.ordinal to setVibrationType(int).
The README says these profiles come from the stock Notes app.

FUNCTION_VIBRATION = 1

records.title: Haptic session call sequence (as implemented)
records.summary: The order of calls the repository's client makes to turn Stylo 2 writing feedback on and off.
details: 1. checkSelfPermission(com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT). Stop with PermissionDenied if it is not granted.
2. bindService(ACTION_PENCIL_SDK, package com.oplus.ipemanager). If it returns false the service is unavailable.
3. onServiceConnected: compare binder.interfaceDescriptor with com.oplus.ipemanager.sdk.ISdkAidlInterface before calling anything.
4. setVibrationType(preset ordinal).
5. startFeedBackVibration(). The README describes this as turning on writing feedback system-wide; the service handles the pen.
6. stopFeedBackVibration() to turn it off.
7. unbindService(). The current code does this before step 6, which should be swapped.
Connection states exposed to the UI: DISCONNECTED, CONNECTING, CONNECTED_SDK, CONNECTED_WRONG_IFACE, ERROR.
records.basis: OplusPencilSdkClient.kt and MainActivity.kt

records.title: Xiaomi Pencil Engine (PenEngine AAR)
records.summary: Xiaomi's app-facing stylus SDK. It covers input features and gestures, but the published API list has no explicit haptic motor command.
details: Packages: com.miui.penengine.ocr, .estimate, .onestroke, .hover, .posture, .colorpick, .touchfilm, .auth
Capabilities: stroke prediction, one-stroke shape recognition, handwriting recognition, cross-app colour picking, pen rotation and posture, hover preview, Focus Pen Pro touch-button gestures.
Includes authentication classes. Apps must be registered with Xiaomi.
Most useful as an example of how to structure a vendor-neutral, app-facing API.
records.basis: Research inventory, from dev.mi.com.

records.title: MotionEvent stylus data
records.summary: What an app receives from a stylus on any Android device: position, pressure, tilt, orientation, hover distance, tool type and cancellation flags.
details: Tool type per pointer: getToolType(i) returns TOOL_TYPE_STYLUS or TOOL_TYPE_ERASER.
AXIS_PRESSURE: normally 0 to 1, but can exceed 1 depending on calibration. Clamp or normalise.
AXIS_TILT: radians, 0 is perpendicular to the screen, pi/2 is flat.
AXIS_ORIENTATION: radians, 0 to pi clockwise or 0 to -pi counter-clockwise.
AXIS_DISTANCE (API 14): hover distance, 0 is contact. Values vary by maker; don't rely on exact numbers.
Hover actions: ACTION_HOVER_MOVE (API 12), ACTION_HOVER_ENTER and ACTION_HOVER_EXIT (API 14).
Palm rejection: ACTION_CANCEL, and FLAG_CANCELED (API 33) on a pointer-up that was an accidental touch. Undo that pointer's stroke.
Android 14 and later also send stylus button presses as KeyEvents (from the AOSP stylus spec).
Nothing in MotionEvent controls feedback. It is input only.
records.basis: Android developer guide and MotionEvent reference, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: InputDevice sources and per-device services
records.summary: How an app learns what an input device is and what it offers, including the only standard hook for vibrators on input devices.
details: SOURCE_STYLUS (API 14): the device is a stylus pointing source.
SOURCE_BLUETOOTH_STYLUS (API 23): a Bluetooth stylus.
getMotionRange(axis): the real range and resolution of each axis, such as AXIS_PRESSURE.
getBatteryState() (API 31): battery of the input device, if it reports one.
getLightsManager() (API 31): lights on the input device.
getVibratorManager() (API 31): vibrators that belong to the input device. getVibrator() is deprecated since API 31.
No source has been found showing a stylus motor exposed through getVibratorManager().
records.basis: InputDevice reference, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Vibrator, VibratorManager and VibrationEffect
records.summary: Android's haptics API. It drives the tablet's or phone's own actuator, not a stylus.
details: createOneShot(ms, amplitude) and createWaveform(timings, amplitudes, repeat): API 26. Amplitude 1 to 255 or DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE (-1).
createPredefined(id), API 29: EFFECT_CLICK 0, EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK 1, EFFECT_TICK 2, EFFECT_HEAVY_CLICK 5.

startComposition(), API 30, with primitives: CLICK 1, THUD 2 (API 31), SPIN 3 (API 31), QUICK_RISE 4, SLOW_RISE 5, QUICK_FALL 6, TICK 7, LOW_TICK 8 (API 31). Check support with Vibrator.arePrimitivesSupported().
Duration targets used by Android for estimates: CLICK 12 ms, TICK 5 ms, LOW_TICK 12 ms, QUICK_FALL 100 ms, QUICK_RISE 150 ms, SPIN 150 ms, THUD 300 ms, SLOW_RISE 500 ms.

API 36 adds composition delay types (DELAY_TYPE_PAUSE, DELAY_TYPE_RELATIVE_START_OFFSET), createRepeatingEffect(), and envelope builders (BasicEnvelopeBuilder, WaveformEnvelopeBuilder) for more consistent feel across devices.
VibratorManager (API 31) lists the device's vibrators. InputDevice.getVibratorManager() returns one for an input device.
records.basis: VibrationEffect and Composition reference, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Android Bluetooth stylus HID descriptor
records.summary: The HID report a Bluetooth stylus sends so Android can merge it with touchscreen input.
details: Digitizer usage page, Pen and Stylus usages.
Tip Pressure, 10-bit (0 to 1023) in the example.
1-bit Barrel Switch, Secondary Barrel Switch, Tip Switch and Invert (eraser end).
Transducer Serial Number as a 128-bit feature report.
The descriptor may declare any subset of these, as long as it matches what the pen reports.
May also carry battery level and charging status.
Defines no output report for haptics.
records.basis: AOSP stylus page, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Low-latency inking libraries
records.summary: Jetpack libraries that cut perceived pen latency. Haptics should line up with these strokes, so they matter for timing.
details: androidx.graphics:graphics-core: GLFrontBufferedRenderer draws the live stroke straight to the front buffer, then commit() redraws normally on ACTION_UP. Android 10 (API 29) and later.
View.requestUnbufferedDispatch(event): deliver motion events as soon as they arrive instead of batched per frame.
androidx.input:input-motionprediction: MotionEventPredictor.record() and predict() fill the gap with predicted points. Replace them with real data when it arrives.
Ink API (androidx.ink): brushes, stroke rendering, geometry and storage.
ML Kit Digital Ink Recognition: handwriting to text and gesture recognition.
Latency sources named by Google: pen registration with the touchscreen, touch sampling rate (60 to 1000 Hz), app processing, rendering.
records.basis: Advanced stylus features guide, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Windows pen haptics API (PenDevice + SimpleHapticsController)
records.summary: App-side model: get the pen from a pointer event, pick a named waveform it supports, send it, and stop when the pointer leaves.
details: Classes: PenDevice, SimpleHapticsController, KnownSimpleHapticsControllerWaveforms. In the Windows App SDK, PenDeviceInterop.FromPointerPoint().

Inking waveforms play continuously while the pen touches the screen: InkContinuous (required, fallback), BrushContinuous, PencilContinuous, MarkerContinuous, ChiselMarkerContinuous, EraserContinuous, GalaxyPenContinuous.
Interaction waveforms: Click (required, fallback), Error, Hover, Press, Release, Success, BuzzContinuous, RumbleContinuous.
Pick from SupportedFeedback, then SendHapticFeedback(waveform) or SendHapticFeedback(waveform, intensity).
Call StopFeedback() on PointerExited. Some pens stop on lift by themselves, but not all.
Optional settings, each with a support check: intensity, play count, play duration, replay pause interval.
Windows 11 only. Check that the SimpleHapticsController property exists before using it.
records.basis: Microsoft Learn page, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Windows haptic pen device contract
records.summary: How a pen exposes its motor to the host over plain HID, and how continuous textures start and stop.
details: Transport: HID over Bluetooth with Windows inbox drivers.
Top-level collection: Digitizers page 0x0D, Stylus usage 0x20, containing a Simple Haptic Controller collection (page 0x0E, usage 0x01).

Identity: the digitizer and the Bluetooth stylus collection must both report Transducer Serial Number (0x0D/0x5B, 32-bit, optional Part 2 at 0x6E) and Transducer Vendor ID (0x0D/0x91). This lets the OS tell which pen made which stroke. It is mandatory for haptics.
Discovery: a GET_FEATURE report lists the supported waveforms and their durations (Waveform List 0x10, Duration List 0x11). Continuous waveforms have duration 0.
Command: an OUTPUT report sets Manual Trigger (0x21) to an ordinal, plus optional Intensity 0 to 100 (0x23), Repeat Count (0x24), Retrigger Period (0x25) and Waveform Cutoff Time (0x28).
Ordinal 1 is None and 2 is Stop. Ordinals from 3 index the device's waveform list.

A discrete waveform plays immediately. A continuous waveform is configured and then played at the pen's discretion, for example when it detects tip contact. Microsoft notes this departs from the HID spec because Windows does not use Auto Trigger.
States: Playing, Paused (configured, not touching), Stopped. Clearing the configuration when the pen leaves range is recommended.
The pen digitizer protocol is left open. A protocol with an uplink from screen to pen can be used to modulate the haptics.
Optional tail button over Bluetooth LE keyboard reports: WIN+F20 click, WIN+F19 double-click, WIN+F18 press and hold.
records.basis: Microsoft Haptic Pen Implementation Guide, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: HID Haptics usage page (0x0E)
records.summary: The standard HID vocabulary for haptic waveforms and controls, with the IDs Windows pens use.
details: Controls: Simple Haptic Controller 0x01, Waveform List 0x10, Duration List 0x11, Auto Trigger 0x20, Manual Trigger 0x21, Auto Trigger Associated Control 0x22, Intensity 0x23, Repeat Count 0x24, Retrigger Period 0x25, Waveform Cutoff Time 0x28.
Discrete waveforms: None 0x1001, Stop 0x1002, Click 0x1003, Press 0x1006, Release 0x1007, Hover 0x1008, Success 0x1009, Error 0x100A, Collide 0x1012, Align 0x1013, Step 0x1014, Grow 0x1015.

Continuous waveforms: BuzzContinuous 0x1004, RumbleContinuous 0x1005, InkContinuous 0x100B, PencilContinuous 0x100C, MarkerContinuous 0x100D, ChiselMarkerContinuous 0x100E, BrushContinuous 0x100F, EraserContinuous 0x1010, SparkleContinuous 0x1011.
Required for Windows haptic pens: None, Stop, Click and InkContinuous. Press and Release come as a pair, as do Success and Error.
0x1012 to 0x1015 were added by the HUTRR118 expansion.
The app API calls 0x1011 GalaxyPenContinuous; the hardware guide calls it SparkleContinuous. Both describe a multi-coloured special brush.
records.basis: Microsoft haptic pen and input haptics guides, read on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: UICanvasFeedbackGenerator (iPadOS)
records.summary: Apple's event-based canvas haptics: the app reports what happened, the system decides how it feels.
details: Available from iOS and iPadOS 17.5.
alignmentOccurred(at:): an object snapped to a guide.
pathCompleted(at:): a path finished or a shape was recognised.
Plays on Apple Pencil Pro with a compatible iPad. Playback is not guaranteed; the system weighs device, app state and battery.
There is no continuous texture API. That is the opposite of the OnePlus and Windows inking model.
records.basis: Apple documentation via search results, 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: A haptic stylus is three subsystems
records.summary: Position comes through the screen, extra data and commands go over Bluetooth, and a motor in the pen plays the feel. The OS joins them into one pointer.
details: Position: the tablet's touch controller or digitizer senses the tip and reports coordinates, usually with hover and tilt. xiaomi-sheng-thp reads these from the touch controller frames.

Side channel: a Bluetooth LE link carries what the screen cannot sense, such as buttons, battery, often pressure, settings and haptic commands. Xiaomi pressure arrives as Bluetooth HID; the OnePlus service talks to the pen over Bluetooth; Windows haptic pens use HID over Bluetooth.
Actuator: a small motor (the Stylo 2 has a linear motor) and its driver chip in the pen play the waveform locally.
Joining them: Android correlates timing between touch input and Bluetooth stylus data. Windows matches the transducer serial number and vendor ID reported on both channels.
Consequence: pressure and tilt reach apps through standard Android APIs, but haptics travel the Bluetooth side channel, which on Android belongs to a vendor service.
Before any of this works, the magnetic charger has to hand the pen's Bluetooth address to the tablet. That attach handshake runs through the CPS8601 charger chip.
records.basis: Combined from the verified Xiaomi, OnePlus, AOSP and Microsoft sources.

records.title: How the screen senses a pen
records.summary: The main pen sensing technologies and where haptics fit in each.
details: EMR (electromagnetic resonance): a sensor layer behind the display powers a coil in the pen, so the pen needs no battery. Used by Wacom and Samsung's S Pen. A battery-free pen cannot run a haptic motor.
Active capacitive (active electrostatic): a battery pen transmits from its tip and the touch sensor picks it up. Some protocols also send data from the screen to the pen.
Protocols: Wacom AES, Microsoft Pen Protocol (MPP), USI (open standard), and vendor protocols from Apple, Huawei, Xiaomi, OnePlus and Lenovo (LPP).
Verified for USI: version 2.0 (2022) added NFC wireless charging, in-cell panel support and more tilt. No public source shows haptics in USI.
Verified for Windows: Microsoft says a pen protocol with a screen-to-pen uplink may be used to modulate haptics, but does not require it.
records.basis: Background knowledge, with USI and Microsoft points checked.

records.title: Android's input path for a stylus
records.summary: From pen tip to MotionEvent: firmware, kernel, EventHub, InputReader, InputDispatcher, app window.
details: 1. Device firmware sends HID reports or interrupts over USB, I2C, SPI or Bluetooth.
2. A kernel driver decodes them into Linux input events on an evdev node (/dev/input/eventN).
3. EventHub opens each evdev device and reads raw events.
4. InputReader converts them by device class into Android events and tracks button state. Input device configuration (IDC) files tune per-device behaviour.
5. For a separate Bluetooth stylus, the platform correlates its pressure and buttons with touchscreen contacts (in AOSP this is ExternalStylusInputMapper).
6. InputDispatcher delivers the event to the focused window, where the app sees a MotionEvent.
Every step runs in one direction, toward the app. No step carries feedback back to the pen.
records.basis: AOSP input and stylus pages, read on 2 Nov 2026. The mapper class name is from AOSP source.

records.title: Where Android haptics go, and where they don't
records.summary: Android's haptics stack ends at the device's own motor or at input devices like gamepads. Nothing standard reaches a stylus motor.
details: Standard path: app, Vibrator or VibratorManager, the system vibrator service, the Vibrator HAL, the tablet's own actuator.
View.performHapticFeedback() uses the same path with system-defined feedback constants.
InputDevice.getVibratorManager() (API 31) exposes vibrators that belong to an input device, such as a game controller's rumble motors.
The AOSP stylus spec defines no haptics output, and no source shows a stylus motor through either path.
So stylus haptics on Android are vendor-specific: OnePlus, Xiaomi and Huawei each use their own system software.
Playing the tablet's own vibrator instead is not equivalent. The plan is to report a missing capability, not imitate it.
records.basis: Combined from verified Android references and the AOSP stylus spec.

records.title: The vendor-service pattern
records.summary: On Android, a privileged vendor app owns the pen's Bluetooth link and offers a Binder service. Only apps the vendor trusts may bind.
details: The system service keeps the Bluetooth LE connection to the pen. Ordinary apps cannot use that link.
It publishes a bound service with an AIDL interface: state queries, commands, callbacks.
Access is gated by a system permission ordinary apps cannot hold, and sometimes by vendor authentication of the calling app.
First-party apps and approved partners get access; everyone else is refused.
Verified for OnePlus (com.oplus.ipemanager). Xiaomi's SDK includes an auth package, which suggests a similar gate. Not established for Huawei or Lenovo.
Design consequence: a cross-vendor library needs one adapter per vendor service, and it must say clearly when the current app has no access.
records.basis: Combined from the OnePlus code and README and the Xiaomi SDK package list.

records.title: Continuous textures and discrete events
records.summary: Pen haptics come in two kinds: a texture that plays while writing and short one-off events. The pen plays textures itself on contact.
details: Continuous: the app picks a tool texture, then turns feedback on; the pen vibrates while the tip touches the screen. Windows: InkContinuous, PencilContinuous and others, played at the pen's discretion on contact. OnePlus: setVibrationType(preset), then startFeedBackVibration() and stopFeedBackVibration().

Discrete: short events such as click, hover, align or success. Windows and HID have named waveforms. Apple has alignmentOccurred and pathCompleted. OnePlus may use startVibration(int) here, but that is unconfirmed.

Why textures run in the pen: a Bluetooth round trip is too slow and uneven to time each pulse to each stroke sample. Sending which texture to use and letting the pen start and stop on contact avoids that. Microsoft's rule that continuous waveforms play at the device's discretion fits this explanation.
API consequence: a common library should expose "set texture, enable, disable" separately from "play event", not one vibrate call.
records.basis: Microsoft guides (verified) compared with the OnePlus interface (verified). The explanation is inferred.

records.title: Cross-platform effect mapping
records.summary: A first mapping between OnePlus presets, HID and Windows waveforms, Apple events and Android tablet primitives.
details: Ballpoint: OnePlus BALLPEN (2) = HID InkContinuous 0x100B.
Pencil: OnePlus PENCIL (0) = HID PencilContinuous 0x100C.
Eraser: OnePlus ERASER (1) = HID EraserContinuous 0x1010.
Pen: OnePlus PEN (3) = probably InkContinuous or BrushContinuous 0x100F. Needs testing.
Marker and highlighter: no OnePlus preset. HID MarkerContinuous 0x100D, ChiselMarkerContinuous 0x100E.
Special brush: no OnePlus preset. HID SparkleContinuous 0x1011 (Windows GalaxyPenContinuous).
Snap to guide: HID Align 0x1013 = Apple alignmentOccurred(at:). No known OnePlus equivalent.
Shape recognised: HID Success 0x1009 = Apple pathCompleted(at:).
Click: HID Click 0x1003. OnePlus FUNCTION_VIBRATION (4) is a candidate. On the tablet itself: Android PRIMITIVE_CLICK.
Stop: OnePlus stopFeedBackVibration() = Windows StopFeedback() = HID Stop 0x1002.
records.basis: Inferred from the names and descriptions of verified constants.

records.title: Matching a pen to its strokes
records.summary: Before the host can send feedback to a pen, it must know which Bluetooth device made which stroke. A serial number reported on both channels makes the link.
details: Windows: Transducer Serial Number (0x0D/0x5B) and Transducer Vendor ID (0x0D/0x91) must appear in both the digitizer reports and the Bluetooth stylus collection. Required for haptics and for multi-pen apps.
Android: the AOSP example stylus descriptor includes a 128-bit Transducer Serial Number feature report, and the platform correlates stylus data with touch timing.
On OnePlus the vendor service handles this internally. Apps never see a pen identifier.
records.basis: Microsoft haptic pen guide and AOSP stylus page.

records.title: Observing a stylus on your own device
records.summary: Read-only commands and settings for seeing how the pen shows up on the Pad 3, without changing anything.
details: adb shell getevent -lp: list input devices with their axes and ranges (for example ABS_PRESSURE, ABS_TILT_X).
adb shell getevent -lt /dev/input/eventN: live raw events with timestamps.
adb shell dumpsys input: Android's view of each device, including sources, motion ranges and stylus fusion state.
adb shell dumpsys vibrator_manager: the vibrators the system knows about (Android 12 and later).
adb shell dumpsys package com.oplus.ipemanager: declared services, intent filters and permissions of the pen service.
Developer options, Enable Bluetooth HCI snoop log: record a session with OnePlus Notes, then open the log in Wireshark to see which Bluetooth traffic accompanies haptics.
In an app: InputDevice.getMotionRange(MotionEvent.AXIS_PRESSURE) shows the pressure range and resolution apps actually get.
records.basis: Standard Android tooling. Not run on the Pad 3 yet.

records.title: Proposed architecture: common pen haptics API
records.summary: Apps ask for semantic effects; a shared core picks and times them; one adapter per vendor talks to the pen.
details: Layer 1, app: requests semantic effects (tool texture on or off, discrete events).
Layer 2, common pen haptics API (Rust in the research proposal): profiles, effect selection, timing, state, errors.
Layer 3, vendor adapters: OnePlus (Oplus SDK or Binder service), Xiaomi (Pencil Engine, once a haptic interface is verified), Lenovo (LPP, if documented), Huawei (NearLink, if documented).
Layer 4: the pen's own actuator.
Report unsupported capabilities explicitly. Don't imitate them with the tablet's vibrator.
Model the effect vocabulary on the HID Haptics page and the Windows waveform names, which are already vendor-neutral.
records.basis: Research inventory section 7, extended with the verified Windows model.

records.title: Reusability assessment
records.summary: Which components can be shared across vendors and which must stay vendor-specific.
details: Android stylus input: high reuse. Use the standard Android APIs.
Pressure and tilt processing: high reuse. Shared Rust or Kotlin implementation.
Haptic effect definitions: high reuse. Vendor-neutral effect model.
Xiaomi Pencil Engine: low reuse across vendors. Study its API structure.
Oplus Binder integration: OnePlus only. Dedicated adapter.
Xiaomi Bluetooth and HID implementation: Xiaomi only. Protocol-analysis reference.
Lenovo LPP and Huawei NearLink: unknown. Research separately.
records.basis: Research inventory section 7.

records.title: oplus_wireless_pen kernel driver
records.summary: Kernel module for the pen's magnetic wireless charger (CPS8601). It detects attach and passes the pen's Bluetooth address on for pairing.
details: File: /vendor/lib/modules/oplus_wireless_pen.ko
Descriptions: "Wireless Pen Charger Cps8601" and "QTI Glink wireless pen driver". Licence GPL v2.

Depends on panel_event_notifier, oplus_bsp_boot_projectinfo and pmic_glink. The project-info dependency suggests it selects firmware by hardware variant.

records.title: cps8601_firmware.bin (pen charger firmware)
records.summary: 15 KB firmware for the tablet-side pen charging chip. It covers power transfer and the pen's in-band packets, with nothing about haptics.
details: Path: /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/<number>/cps8601_firmware.bin. Numbers seen: 23926, 23927, 23976, 23978, 24926.

Every copy is 15,360 bytes. The 239xx copies share SHA-256 cfac67370d543b8b31a914a240dca5b043743388da539465260e6df6400f9e81. 24926 has 33a4ab21db5e92af7f144fecf3d86f64137079d22e4890902d6da24dd6aa1ee4.
Looks like 8051 code: long jumps at the reset, INT0 and Timer0 vector slots (0x0000, 0x0003, 0x000B), and Keil C51 %bu format strings.
The strings show a Qi-style transmitter: cmd enter tx mode, Ping:Freq=…, ploss fod trigger, q cali, save Q value, RX remove, low power, start crc check, equipment (factory) mode, ver%bu.%bu.
No strings about vibration, haptics or Bluetooth.
The directory numbers look like Oplus project numbers for each hardware variant. Inferred, not confirmed.
records.basis: Files from the cxzlw repo, hashed and string-scanned on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Pen attach handshake: charging link to Bluetooth pairing
records.summary: When the pen snaps on, the charger chip receives the pen's Bluetooth LE address over the charging link. That starts pairing, so it must succeed before any haptics can work.
details: 1. The magnetic charger detects the pen (Rx attach!) and starts transmitting power (tx wakeup!).
2. The pen answers by modulating the charging load (Qi ASK packets: receive ask pkt!).
3. One packet carries the pen's Bluetooth LE address (get ble addr). The driver validates it and reports it.
4. The accessory service then presumably pairs over Bluetooth LE. Haptic commands from com.oplus.ipemanager use that link.
On converted tablets the charger firmware for the hardware's directory is missing, so step 2 or 3 fails and the pen never pairs.
Fixes: provide the missing firmware directories (overlay module), or flash the matching region's odm.img. Results vary.
Useful for capture: attaching the pen marks the moment Bluetooth LE pairing should begin in an HCI snoop log.
Full write-up: research/pen-attach-handshake.md
records.basis: Kernel log and findings in the cxzlw README; the sequence and its link to haptics are inferred.
